## What

Rebalance `shape:idea` so its primary job at intake is refining the idea — sharpening the problem, drawing out what the person actually means, surfacing assumptions and unknowns — instead of first scoring how valuable the idea is.

Today the skill opens with ICE scoring and confidence/Kano classification. That value judgement has its place, but it shouldn't come first: a raw idea is usually under-articulated, so the move with the most payoff is to interrogate and clarify it with the person before valuing it. Scoring a vague idea only paints a confident-looking number on a fuzzy input.

So intake becomes a short, pointed interview, not a scoring form:

* lead with a best-guess read of the idea and a confidence number on that read;
* ask one sharp question at a time, each carrying its own best guess;
* reflect the idea back;
* catch "should-want" framing;
* surface assumptions.

The loop ends when the person says yes to a six-line restate in their own words. Only then does the skill take evidence, write the A2 statement, and route. A score appears only if the person asks to rank this idea against others.

The artefact at `docs/idea-bank/<slug>.md` leads with Raw intake → Refined intent (confirmed restate, assumptions, open questions) before evidence and routing. The ICE table appears only when the optional scoring step ran.

## Why

* A premature scoring framework rewards ideas that are easy to score, not ideas that are well-understood. It can also anchor the conversation on a number instead of the problem.
* The real bottleneck at intake is articulation, not ranking. Refine first; score (if at all) once the idea is actually sharp.

## Inspiration

* `agent-skills:idea-refine` — focuses on iteratively sharpening an idea rather than judging it.
* `agent-skills:interview-me` — interview-style elicitation that draws the idea out of the person through questions.

Pull the elicitation/refinement posture from these into `shape:idea`: ask clarifying questions, reflect the idea back, expose assumptions and gaps — and treat scoring as a lighter, later, optional step rather than the spine of the skill.

## Scope notes

* This is a posture/sequencing change to `skills/idea/SKILL.md` (and its references), not a new skill.
* Preserve the existing routing gates (problem-vs-solution check, baseline check, route the idea); the change is about what the skill spends its effort on before routing.
* Decide deliberately whether ICE/Kano stays as an optional tail step or is dropped — don't keep it as the default opening move.

## Technical specification

Full spec lives in the planning artefact; the critical detail to execute is below.

### Confirmed decisions

* **ICE/Kano → optional tail step.** Confidence (Gilad evidence quality) stays load-bearing — the routing gate keys off it, and assessing *evidence* is distinct from *scoring value*. The full ICE = I×C×E product and the Kano lens demote to an optional step, run only after the idea is sharp and only when a comparative ranking is needed. The artefact's ICE table becomes optional.
* **Elicitation → full interactive loop.** Port `interview-me` faithfully: hypothesis + confidence number, one question at a time each with a guess attached, want-vs-should-want check, restate intent in the user's own words, loop until explicit yes (95% confidence test).

### New workflow sequence (gates preserved)

| # | Step | Change |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | Capture the idea verbatim | unchanged |
| 2 | **Elicit & refine the idea** (NEW spine) | interactive loop; summary + cite to new reference |
| 3 | **Gate: problem or solution?** | kept; lighter (elicitation already surfaced the problem) |
| 4 | Interrogate the evidence → Confidence | kept (incl. baseline check vs `app-context.md`) |
| 5 | Write the problem statement (A2) | kept |
| 6 | **Gate: does the problem statement hold?** | kept |
| 7 | **Gate: route the idea** (Confidence <5 / ≥5) | kept — load-bearing; validation-method table kept |
| 8 | **(Optional) Score ICE / Kano lens** | demoted; run only when comparative ranking needed |
| 9 | Write and file the triage record | kept |
